content_of_post_to_comment:
I know I'm not at my core undisciplined, I've accomplished things I'm really proud of, but every so often I get in years-long ruts where I completely lose faith in my ability to do any hard work.

I have depression (treatment resistant) and autism/maybe ADHD but I'm not saying they are excuses and I'm looking into getting the proper treatment I need now, however, I still feel like advice that is like "Do the opposite of what you feel when you're depressed" and "You can only save yourself" etc., while true, is currently unhelpful because I know doing what I need to do will be very painful at times. And I've convinced myself I'll give up anyways, won't follow through, and am just lazy so I can't do it.

I try to stop ruminating over it but the hold on me is so strong. If I finally broke free of this I know my life would dramatically improve, I just don't know what to do.

Thanks for reading and any advice is appreciated.
comment: I wonder if treating this as a discipline problem is making the rut even harder to escape. When you've spent years expecting yourself to give up, even starting something becomes loaded with the fear of proving yourself right. Maybe the first goal isn't to do hard things consistently, but to rebuild trust in yourself through commitments so small that you can actually keep them, even on bad days.
